reviews.comment: I took this class 2 years ago but i have to come back and rate. this class made me consider dropping out. turns out it was just because of him. he doesn't know anything about 204. every single class i have taken after this one has been easier than his class. good luck. i'm a senior and still don't think i could solve my final exam from that class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Medium hard class made near impossible by a professor who genuinely cannot form a coherent thought. All learning will happen outside of lecture, it is insane how this man managed an ivy league degree while getting all of his own example problems wrong constantly. Use the textbook and slides and do the practice exams 10x times fowards and backwards.
Very nice guy but not a good professor. Tried doing practice problems to help us and ended up getting them wrong himself. Partial credit criteria is very weird. You have to teach yourself everything.

This professor did not understand the material. He admitted 3x in class to writing the slides using AI and using AI before class to teach/explain the material to him so he could attempt to explain it to us. He lacked clear communication as 70% of his (too quiet) speech is umms and uhs. Tiny mistakes on exams cost whole final grade percentages each.

class itself is already pretty hard if you don't have a good grasp on chemistry, prof doesn't have a good basis on the info. he's presenting. exam score distribution is INSANE. one question will have 60 points and the other two split the 40.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Shin seems like a nice guy but I didn't learn anything in the lectures. He'd often get confused and get example questions wrong in class, and one time he said he “didn't really get” a concept so he used ChatGPT to write the slides. The material isn't that bad, but it's hard to understand anything he teaches. The TAs were way more helpful.
Cannot string together a coherent sentence and doesn't understand the material he teaches. Literally is not capable of teaching

Confuses himself, reliant on AI for everything, sounds unsure of himself when teaching, "writes" work on MS notepad, spends all class on one problem just to get it completely wrong, teaches like he's seeing the material for the first time, slides are often incoherent - info just appears out of nowhere. Nice guy but you'll teach yourself. good luck

Shin gets his own practice problems wrong half the time, does not write/draw out his work, instead typing on a microsoft notepad, confusing himself and giving up... skipping the entire problem entirely. Hilarious in that you will be laughing AT him, inspirational in that if this guy can get a job as a prof, then you can be anything you aspire to.
